conceptZh: 玩具機器人翻著一本厚書越看越入迷，頭一點一點地開始打瞌睡，書慢慢滑下來蓋在他臉上；他就這樣睡著發出小小的呼聲，每呼一次就有一頁被吹得掀起來又落下。
object: a small toy robot and a thick picture book
morph: the glyph 書 stands still as a solid sculpture while the robot falls asleep under the book
creativeAngle: 孩子看漫畫看到睡著是很有共鳴的畫面，笑點用「每呼一次就掀一頁」的小細節收尾，安靜卻很好笑，也和其他支的大動作形成節奏對比。書為聿在上、曰在下共十畫，橫畫多容易糊，字體靜止並要求橫畫等距。語音詞「看書」，看在此念ㄎㄢˋ、書ㄕㄨ，避開照看的ㄎㄢ。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second 3D stylized toy animation as one continuous locked-off shot on a clean solid pale butter cream background. One correctly formed Traditional Chinese character 書 stands centered the whole time as a flat-fronted sculpture in saturated deep navy, filling about 70% of the frame height with comfortable margins on all sides. Use standard textbook proportions: the brush-shaped 聿 on top sits above the 曰 below, clearly separated, with every horizontal stroke evenly spaced and never merging. The glyph never moves, rotates, tilts or gets covered, and the camera stays locked. At its base sits a small boxy toy robot with a thick picture book open on his knees. From 0.5 seconds he reads with real interest, turning a page, leaning in. At 1.4 seconds his head dips, and snaps back up. He blinks hard and carries on. At 2.0 seconds it dips again, lower, and comes back up more slowly. At 2.6 seconds his arms sag and the book slides gently up over his face and settles there like a little tent. He does not move. Beat. From 3.2 seconds, tiny soft snores begin, and with each one a single page lifts up off the book and drops back down, in a slow steady rhythm. Hold on that quiet joke through 4.2 seconds, then the sleeping robot and his book slide gently out of frame to the left by 4.6 seconds. From 4.7 seconds to 8.0 seconds the frame is completely still and clean, holding on the single centered 書 with nothing else in shot. Style: Pixar-like glossy chunky toy materials, soft studio lighting, bright high-contrast colors that are vivid but never neon, no dark or moody grading, no white blowouts. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin and says exactly 「書、書、看書」, using the reading ㄕㄨ for 書 both on its own and inside the word. Speak the first 書 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 2.0 seconds, and 看書 around 5.6 seconds while the finished glyph is held still, with natural pauses, then stop; do not keep chanting the character or repeat the line. Keep every sound effect soft and clear of the voice, and use no music louder than the voice. The spoken word is audio only and must not be added to the picture. The only writing anywhere in the frame is the single character 書: no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no other letters, numbers, watermarks, scenery, extra props, particles, lens flare, motion blur on the glyph, or flashing effects.

conceptZh: 披風英雄的長披風跟著他翻書的動作，慢一拍就把書頁攪亂，最後書頁剛好疊成「書」。
object: caped action-figure hero, an oversized cape, a thick storybook
morph: flying pages settle into the strokes of 書
creativeAngle: 披風慢一拍模仿主角每個動作，造成翻頁的小混亂。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second animated comedy, locked frontal camera. Setting: a warm coral reading nook with a pale-cream floor; the glyph is deep forest-green paper-craft strokes standing at center. A caped action-figure hero (an original toy with a plain teal cape three sizes too long) stands at right holding a thick book. The Traditional Chinese glyph 書 stays centered and uncropped at about 70% of frame height with generous margins. Moment one (0.0-1.8s): the hero opens the big book with a flourish, and a beat later the cape flips open too and flops over his head; the first 書 is spoken as the cover opens. Moment two (1.8-3.5s): he flips a page and the cape flips one beat late, whipping pages into the air; they flutter, fold and snap into the horizontal bars and vertical strokes of 書 at center; the second 書 is spoken as the final page lands. Moment three (3.5-5.0s): he tries to look cool, but the cape sweeps a small school bag off a shelf onto his shoulders; 書包 is spoken as the bag lands with a soft bounce. From 5.0-8.0s the glyph 書 is perfectly still and unobstructed; the cape still mimics each pose a beat late: he points, then the cape points; the glyph is untouched. Audio: one warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks slowly and distinctly in Taiwan-standard Mandarin, reading exactly these syllables with clear tones and no erhua: 「書、書、書包」 (ㄕㄨ、ㄕㄨ、ㄕㄨ ㄅㄠ). Timing: first utterance at about 0.5s, second at about 2.5s, the word at about 4.4s; then stop, no repeats and no extra speech. Beneath the voice only page flutters and cloth swishes, no music. The single glyph is the only on-screen text; the vocabulary stays audio-only with no subtitles, watermark, clutter or flashing.

conceptZh: 浣熊助手花生抱著搖搖晃晃的書塔，踮著腳偷偷去拿打瞌睡布忍者守著的最後一本書；每一步都吱吱叫，就差一點點時，布忍者突然睜眼，兩個面對面大叫，煙霧彈砰地炸開，書塔飛上天，一本本書落下來疊成「書」。最後布忍者躲進小書包裡卻露出整顆頭，花生還對著書包敬禮。
object: Peanut the cartoon raccoon with a wobbling tower of navy books and one tall navy brush, a dozing felt ninja guarding the last book, and a small red school bag
morph: the scream-and-smoke-bomb collision launches the book tower; the flat books drop as the evenly spaced horizontal strokes, the brush lands upright as the central vertical, and the bottom books close into the 曰 box, forming a solid navy 書 in standard form
creativeAngle: 前兩版都是安靜的看書或披風慢半拍，這次改成清楚的「偷拿—嚇到—撞成字」身體喜劇：花生的書塔本身就是筆畫材料，撞擊把書甩成「書」，小朋友一看就懂因果。布忍者躲進書包還露出頭，正好讓「書包」這個詞在說出口時有具體又好笑的畫面；花生在錯誤時機敬禮，守住他的人設。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second 3D stylized toy-animation comedy as one continuous locked-off frontal shot on a clean solid pale butter-yellow background with a slightly warmer flat floor line, nothing else behind. Only two characters ever appear plus one prop. The lead is Peanut, an original cartoon raccoon sidekick with a round belly, a striped tail and big eager eyes, carrying a wobbling tower of flat navy books stacked far too tall for him, with one long navy paintbrush poking out of the top. The buddy is a tiny felt ninja in a plain grey hood, dozing on the right side of the frame on top of one golden book, "hidden" behind a single green leaf far too small to cover him, snoring with a little bubble.

Moment one, want it (0.0 to 1.6 seconds): Peanut shuffles in from the left under his swaying tower, stops, spots the golden book under the sleeping ninja, and his eyes go wide and sparkly. He points at it with his whole arm, the tower tilts dangerously, and he catches it with his tail. The first 書 is spoken at about 0.6 seconds right as he points at the golden book.

Moment two, try and miss (1.6 to 3.2 seconds): Peanut tiptoes toward the ninja with huge exaggerated high knees. Every step makes a loud rubber squeak and the ninja twitches without waking; Peanut freezes mid-step on one foot each time, tower leaning, then continues. On the third squeak he reaches the ninja, stretches one paw toward the golden book, fingers an inch from it, tongue out in concentration.

Moment three, the big crash (3.2 to 4.4 seconds): the ninja's eyes snap open. A frozen half-beat of the two faces nose to nose. Both scream in silly cartoon voices, the ninja fumbles a smoke bomb that pops instantly in a soft puff of pale blue cloud, and the two bonk foreheads with a squash-and-stretch wobble. The impact launches Peanut's whole tower straight up. The books come down fast and land as the strokes: the flat books drop one by one as the evenly spaced horizontal bars of the top part, the long brush plants upright as the central vertical stroke through them, and the bottom books click together into the closed 曰 box underneath. By 4.4 seconds the pieces have become one correctly formed Traditional Chinese character 書 in solid saturated deep navy, standing centered and uncropped, filling about 70% of the frame height with clear margins, with standard textbook proportions: 聿 on top clearly separated from 曰 below, every horizontal stroke evenly spaced and never merging, the vertical stroke straight and centered. The second 書 is spoken at about 4.2 seconds exactly as the last stroke snaps into place.

Moment four, payoff and hold (4.4 to 8.0 seconds): the glyph 書 stays perfectly still, clean and unobstructed through the end of the clip, never touched, covered, tilted or moved. Beside it on the lower right sits a small red school bag. At about 4.8 seconds the dazed felt ninja scrambles over and dives into the bag to hide, but his whole head and the bag's flap stick out in plain view; he holds very still, convinced he is invisible. The word 書包 is spoken at about 5.4 seconds exactly as the bag with the ninja's head poking out is clearly on screen. Peanut, still dizzy with little stars circling his head, wobbles to the lower left, then snaps a proud salute at the school bag at exactly the wrong moment, loses his balance, sits down on his tail and grins happily at the finished 書 through 8.0 seconds, never crossing in front of the strokes.

Style: Pixar-like chunky glossy toy materials with a soft felt texture on the ninja, soft even studio lighting, bright high-contrast colors that are vivid but never neon, no white blowouts, no dark grading, no motion blur on the glyph, no flashing effects.

Audio: one warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks slowly and distinctly in clear Taiwan-standard Mandarin, reading exactly these syllables with clear tones and no erhua: 「書、書、書包」 (ㄕㄨ、ㄕㄨ、ㄕㄨ ㄅㄠ). First 書 at about 0.6 seconds, second 書 at about 4.2 seconds, 書包 at about 5.4 seconds while the finished glyph is held still; then stop, with no repeats and no other speech. Under the voice only light rubber squeaks, a soft pop for the smoke bomb, a cartoon bonk and gentle book thumps, all quieter than the voice, no music. The vocabulary word is audio only. The single glyph 書 is the only text anywhere in the frame: no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no letters, numbers, watermarks, scenery, extra props or clutter.
